title: 2023 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final
text:
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox football match | title = 2023 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final | image = | event = [[2023 Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = [[File:Colours of Clare.svg|border|40px]] {{GG|Clare|hurling}} | team1association = | team1score = 1–22 | team2 = [[File:Colours of Limerick.svg|border|40px]] {{GG|Limerick|hurling}} | team2association = | team2score = 1–23 | details = | date = 11 June 2023 | stadium = [[Gaelic Grounds]] | city = [[Limerick]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Aaron Gillane]] (Limerick) | referee = Liam Gordon (Galway) | attendance = 43,756 | weather = Sunny | previous = [[2022 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2022]] | next = [[2024 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2024]] }} The '''2023 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match that was played on 11 June at the [[Gaelic Grounds]] in [[Limerick]]. It was contested by [[2022 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|defending]] champions [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] and [[Clare county hurling team|Clare]].{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0530/1386460-limerick-gain-home-advantage-for-munster-final/|title=Limerick gain home advantage for Munster final|date=30 May 2023|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=31 May 2023}}{{cite web|url= https://munster.gaa.ie/event/2023-munster-senior-hurling-championship-final/|title=2023 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final – Limerick V Clare – Venue Confirmed / Ticket Details|date=30 May 2023|work=Munster GAA|accessdate=31 May 2023}} The game was televised live on [[RTÉ 2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'', presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]], with analysis from [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]], [[Joe Canning]] and [[Shane Dowling (hurler)|Shane Dowling]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Brendan Cummins (GAA player)|Brendan Cummins]]. ==Overview== The two teams were meeting in the Munster final for the second year in a row with Limerick winning the final in [[2022 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2022]] by 1–29 to 0-29 after extra-time.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2022/0605/1303110-limerick-edge-past-clare-in-munster-final-classic/|title=Limerick edge Clare in extra-time epic to win fourth Munster Championship in a row|date=7 June 2022|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=7 April 2023}} Limerick were bidding to win the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster title]] for a fifth successive year and for the 24th time overall with Clare looking for a first Munster title since [[1998 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|1998]] and seventh title. This was the 62nd championship game between the two counties, Limerick having 38 wins to Clare's 21 with two draws, from the previous 61. General sale terrace tickets for the match went on sale on 1 June and sold out within 23 minutes.{{cite web|url= https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/fans-fume-munster-hurling-championship-30130865|title= Fans fume as Munster Hurling Championship final tickets sell-out in 23 minutes|date=1 June 2023|work=Irish Mirror|accessdate=2 June 2023}} All other tickets were allocated to the county boards of the two counties for distribution to the clubs.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0601/1386934-munster-hurling-final-on-course-to-be-a-sellout/ |title= Munster hurling final on course to be a sellout|date=1 June 2023|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=2 June 2023}} ==Match== ===Summary === {{Expand section|date=August 2024}} ===Details=== {{GAAmatchbox |date = 11 June 2023 |time = 13:45 |round = Final |report = [https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/2023/06/11/limerick-earns-narrow-win-over-clare-to-claim-historic-fifth-munster-title-in-a-row/ Report] |team1 = [[File:Colours of Clare.svg|border|20px]] {{GG|Clare|hurling}} |score1 = 1–22 |score2 = 1–23 | aet = |team2 = [[File:Colours of Limerick.svg|border|20px]] {{GG|Limerick|hurling}} |HT = |FT = 1-22 - 1-23 |goals1 = Tony Kelly 0-6 (0-2 frees); Mark Rodgers 1-2; Aidan McCarthy 0-4 (0-3 frees); Shane O’Donnell, David Fitzgerald, Ian Galvin 0-2 each; Cathal Malone, Diarmuid Ryan, Ryan Taylor, Aron Shanagher 0-1 each. |points1 = |goals2 = Aaron Gillane 1-11 (0-8 frees); Tom Morrissey, David Reidy 0-3 each; Cathal O’Neill 0-2; Darragh O’Donovan, Gearoid Hegarty, Kyle Hayes, Adam English 0-1 each. |points2 = |location = [[Limerick]] |venue = [[Gaelic Grounds]] |attendance = 43,756{{cite web |title=LIVE Munster hurling final: Limerick v Clare |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/2023/06/11/live-munster-hurling-final-limerick-v-clare/ |website=Irish Times |access-date=11 June 2023}} |referee = Liam Gordon (Galway)
